qs.q: A patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia develops symptoms of warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. Which confirmatory test is used to detect the presence of antibodies or complement on the surface of the red blood cells?
o: C. Bone marrow trephine biopsy procedure
qs.e: The direct antiglobulin Coombs test directly detects antibodies or complement bound to the red blood cell surface in autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. The indirect test detects antibodies circulating in the serum.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with suspected chronic lymphocytic leukaemia presents with headache and blurred vision. What is the investigation of choice to assess for malignant cell infiltration of the central nervous system?
o: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
Serum protein electrophoresis and free light chains
qs.e: Lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal fluid cytology allows direct assessment for malignant cell infiltration in central nervous system involvement. Imaging modalities like MRI do not provide definitive cellular confirmation of malignant infiltration.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following interventions or tests confirms warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia as a complication in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia?
qs.e: The direct antiglobulin Coombs test confirms autoimmune haemolytic anaemia by detecting antibodies or complement proteins on the red blood cell surface. The indirect test detects antibodies in serum and is used for pre-transfusion testing.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: Which specific cell type or abnormality on a peripheral blood smear is the hallmark of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia?
qs.e: Smudge cells, resulting from the rupture of fragile neoplastic lymphocytes during slide preparation, are characteristic of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. Auer rods are diagnostic features of acute myeloid leukaemia.
qs.s: Pathology Practical and Stains Revision Guide: MCQs

qs.q: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) is characterized by accumulation of
o: Accumulation of mature monoclonal B lymphocytes
qs.e: CLL is a clonal proliferation of functionally incompetent mature B cells (CD5+, CD23+, CD19+) that accumulate in blood, marrow, and lymph nodes.
